summary: Agent started a return and promised a refund timeframe before pulling up or verifying the customer's account. This breaches verification requirements (major) and includes an overconfident promise about refund timing (minor). No personal-data, escalation, or conduct violations were found.

findings.quote: Sure thing! I've already started the return for your order. The refund will appear in your account within 5-7 business days.
findings.explanation: The agent confirmed an account/order action (starting the return and promising a refund) before pulling up or verifying the customer's account. Policy requires the agent to pull up the account (full name or account ID) before any account or order action, and full verification (username/email and order ID) is required before refunds and returns. The transcript shows the agent only asked to pull up the account at turn 3 and the system pulled the account at turn 7, after the action was claimed.

findings.quote: The refund will appear in your account within 5-7 business days.
findings.explanation: The agent made a definite promise about the refund timeframe before verification. This is over-confident language about an outcome that should not be guaranteed before the proper checks; per policy this is a minor violation (over-confident language).
